newsitem.title: MEXICO: Nortel says it "bullish" on Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Nortel says it "bullish" on Latin America.

text.p: Canada's Northern Telecom Ltd (Nortel) is "bullish" on Latin America and will seek further business as a "full-service supplier" in Mexico in 1997, said Gary Donahee, Nortel's president for the Caribbean and Latin America.

"I can say that we have four major areas in Latin America that we are very bullish on, and that starts with Mexico," Donahee told a news conference in which he introduced the new general director of Nortel de Mexico, Gian Carlo Pecchioni Onofrietti.
Donahee identified the other "strategic areas" that Nortel is most interested in as Colombia, Brazil and the "southern cone" of South America, grouping together Chile and Argentina.
Donahee estimated that eight to 10 percent of Nortel's revenue comes from the Caribbean and Latin American division known as CALA "and we hope to grow that substantially."
The company reported revenues of US$12.85 billion wordlwide in 1996, up 20 percent from 1995 revenues of US$10.67 billion.
"The corporation sees Latin America from an investment perspective as the next China," Donahee said.
Pecchioni was promoted to head of Telnor de Mexico on Jan. 1 after joining the compnay less than a year ago.
"We have doubled our operations year after year and we expect next year to be the same," Pecchioni said. "Our vision for the year 2000 is to be a company with revenues above $500 million."
He said the company hoped to post revenues of $210 million in Mexico in 1997.
Nortel de Mexico has signed major contracts with the former monopoly Telmex as well as one two of its new competitors, the long-distance carrier Avantel and cellular phone company Iusacell.
Its only factory in Latin America is in Monterrey, Mexico, which produced one million telephones for export in 1996, Donahee said.
